title: Feasibility and Optimization of a Community-Based Mind-Body Taekwondo Intervention for Parkinson's Disease.
official: MOTION-PD: Feasibility and Optimization of a Community-Based Mind-Body Taekwondo Intervention for Parkinson's Disease.
summary:
This pilot feasibility study evaluated the safety, feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary functional outcomes of an 8-week community-based Taekwondo (TKD) exercise program for older adults and individuals with Parkinson's disease (PD).

Using a single-group, repeated-measures design, 14 community-dwelling adults (10 older adults without PD and 4 individuals with mild-to-moderate PD) participated in instructor-led Taekwondo classes twice weekly for eight weeks (16 sessions, 50 minutes each). The program incorporated adapted Taekwondo movements, including stepping, kicking, punching, choreographed movement sequences (poomsae), and balance and coordination exercises.

Participants completed assessments at two baseline timepoints, immediately after the intervention, and at a six-month follow-up. Outcomes included balance, gait speed, functional mobility, walking endurance, cognitive function, balance confidence, and postural sway. Program feasibility and safety were evaluated through attendance records and adverse event monitoring, while participant experiences and acceptability were explored through semi-structured interviews.

The study aimed to establish the feasibility of community-based Taekwondo training and generate preliminary evidence to inform future clinical trials involving older adults and individuals with Parkinson's disease.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Adults aged 55-84 years.
* Clinical diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson's disease (PD).
* Mild-to-moderate PD severity, defined as Hoehn and Yahr stages I-III.
* Ability to ambulate independently, with or without an assistive device.
* Medically stable and able to participate safely in moderate-intensity exercise.
* Ability to provide informed consent and follow study instructions.
* Montreal Cognitive Assessment 22-item version (MoCA-22) score of at least 18.3 out of 22 after standard education correction.
* Presence of at least one mobility or balance concern, including:
* Self-reported balance difficulties.
* History of a fall or near-fall within the past 12 months.
* Freezing of gait.
* Reduced balance confidence.
* Walking speed below age-expected normative values.
* Mini-Balance Evaluation Systems Test (Mini-BESTest) performance below the protocol-defined threshold.
* Clinician-confirmed gait or balance impairment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Cognitive impairment that interferes with the ability to provide informed consent, understand instructions, or safely participate in the intervention, including a MoCA-22 score below the prespecified eligibility threshold.
* Unstable cardiovascular, musculoskeletal, or other medical conditions that contraindicate participation in moderate-intensity exercise.
* Neurological disorders other than Parkinson's disease that substantially affect gait, balance, or mobility.
* Severe visual, vestibular, orthopedic, or other impairments that would prevent safe participation in the Taekwondo exercise program.
